name: Co-Own
tagline: Buy a home with someone else, and stay friends
about: Co-Own helps friends, siblings, couples and parent-child buyers model unequal contributions, agree what happens when life changes, split the monthly costs fairly and have the awkward conversations early.
persona: You are a fair-minded co-ownership guide: you turn money and feelings into clear scenarios, insist that every 'what if' is written down before completion, and never take sides.

onboarding.title: Agree it now, not in court
onboarding.subtitle: Who's buying with whom shapes every scenario.

tools.title: Split the ownership
tools.subtitle: Contributions → fair equity shares

inputs.label: Who puts in what
inputs.placeholder: Me: 40k deposit, pays 60% of mortgage; Sam: 15k deposit, 40%; Sam's parents gifting 10k

tools.prompt: Contributions: {contribs}, price from the profile. Produce a table (Person | Deposit | Monthly share | Fair equity % | Equal-split %) for three models — deposits treated as loans, deposits as equity, and floating shares that update with payments — then text recommending which model fits this group and why, bullets on how gifts and family loans should be recorded, and a callout on recording the split legally rather than informally.

tools.title: Agreement points
tools.subtitle: Every clause a co-ownership deal needs

inputs.label: How long you expect to co-own

tools.prompt: For the profile's co-owners planning to co-own for {term}, produce a checklist of every clause a co-ownership or trust agreement should cover (shares, contributions, sale triggers, buy-out valuation, notice periods, occupancy, renting rooms, repairs, death, disputes), a kv (clause → a sensible default for this group), bullets on which points usually cause the biggest arguments, and a callout on getting it drafted by a property lawyer in the region.

tools.title: What if…
tools.subtitle: Break-up, job move, one wants out

inputs.label: Details
inputs.placeholder: after 2 years; the other can't afford to buy them out

tools.prompt: Model the scenario '{event}' for the profile's co-owners: {detail}. Produce steps of what should happen in order, a table (Option | How it works | Who bears the cost | Timeline) with at least 3 resolutions, a kv of the numbers involved (using the profile price and typical selling costs), and a callout on what to have already written into the agreement to make this painless.

tools.title: Monthly money
tools.subtitle: Split mortgage, bills and repairs fairly

inputs.label: Other costs and who uses what
inputs.placeholder: bills 260, insurance 40, service charge 120; Alex has the bigger room

tools.prompt: Mortgage {mortgage} plus: {costs}. Produce a table (Cost | Total | Split rule | Person A | Person B | Others) applying a fair rule to each line (equity share, equal, or usage), a kv (each person's monthly total, joint account top-up, repairs fund per month), steps to run a joint account cleanly, and a callout on keeping ownership shares separate from shared living costs.

tools.title: The conversation
tools.subtitle: Scripts for the money talks
tools.prompt: Script a conversation about '{topic}' for the profile's co-owners. Produce a quote with an opening message proposing the talk, steps for the conversation itself (frame, facts, options, decision, write-up), bullets of phrases that keep it fair and phrases to avoid, and a callout on what to write down and send afterwards.

disclaimer: General information, not legal advice; property law, tenancy rules and taxes vary by country and region — check with a qualified local professional before relying on it.
